name: Christopher Buse
bio: Christopher Buse is SVP and Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) for Old Republic International, where he is responsible for designing and implementing the enterprise security architecture for the company. Buse previously served as Assistant Commissioner and CISO for the State of Minnesota central technology agency, MNIT Services, and in several critical audit and technology systems roles at the Minnesota Office of the Legislative Auditor. Buse graduated from St. Cloud State University in Minnesota with a Bachelor of Science degree in Accounting and has supplemented his degree with numerous computer science and management information systems courses. Christopher is a Certified Public Accountant (inactive), Certified Information Systems Auditor, and a Certified Information Systems Security Professional.

name: Mary Diner
bio: Mary Diner is Director of Ethical Hacking at UnitedHealth Group and has over 25 years of broad security leadership and relationship management at scale, from operations, program and product portfolio management, architecture and engineering in verticals ranging from multiple regulated industries, including manufacturing, financial services and healthcare, in Fortune 500 companies. The secret sauce to her career success is building positive relationships with solutions providers and a passionate focus on business relationships that are collaborative and mutually beneficial. Mary is passionate about finding emerging solutions to the always emerging new security threats and connecting people to attack those problems together. To that end she has been active in the CyberSecurity Summit planning for several years now to help provide meaningful training and valuable professional community. Previous employers have included consulting as well as 3M, Wells and presently Optum.

name: Vincent Aimutis
bio:
Vince Aimutis is the Vice President – Director of Information Services and CISO at Federated Mutual Insurance in Owatonna, Minnesota, where he leads the information security, infrastructure, help desk, client, and platform/middleware teams. Known as a particularly passionate technology enthusiast, his broad experience includes network infrastructure, software development, project management, and other infosec roles.
A "Big" since 2010, Vince helps Federated raise millions of dollars each year for Big Brothers, Big Sisters, and is also a board member to CIOs Against Cancer, which supports American Cancer Society research. Vince is a co-chair to the Evanta CISO Governing Body and serves on several CISO Advisory Councils. Vince is a mentor to both leaders and InfoSec newcomers and thrives on connecting with others. A self-described "major foodie", Vince finds work-life balance through travel, fishing, gardening, and all things cooking/smoking/baking.

name: Lisa Baez
bio: Lisa Baez is the Director of Governance, Risk Management and Compliance at Progressive Leasing. Lisa is an experienced Cybersecurity leader with 26 years of expertise in Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC), and Business Information Security Officer (BISO) roles across various highly regulated industries such as FinTech/Financial Services, Medical Device, Travel & Hospitality, Defense & Aerospace and Retail. She earned a BS from Saint Mary's University of Minnesota and holds the CISSP, AIGP, CIPP US & CA, CRISC, CCSP, and PCIP among other professional certifications. Ms. Baez has received recognition such as the NASA Silver Medal Achievement Award and has contributed as a keynote speaker, panelist, and mentor supporting women in IT & Technology, Cybersecurity education, and charitable causes.

name: Martin Bally
bio: Martin Bally is a global cybersecurity executive and Chief AI Security Strategist at Glow. A former Fortune 500 CISO across fintech, automotive, and CPG, Martin has built enterprise programs spanning IT, OT/ICS, and smart manufacturing. At Glow, he translates operational CISO pain points into product strategy while advising boards on agentic AI, endpoint visibility, and machine-speed threat governance. He bridges business growth and cyber risk to deliver durable enterprise value.

name: Craig Byrkit
bio: Craig Byrkit is Vice President and Information Security Officer at Ameriprise Financial Services, LLC. Previously, he was Global Vice President, Information Security and Data Protection Officer at Reinsurance Group of America with Chief Information Security Officer oversight responsibilities. Before RGA, he was the RGAX Chief Information Security and Privacy Officer and managed global cybersecurity, data privacy, and physical security programs. At Edward Jones, Craig built and led information systems threat and vulnerability management, incident response, privacy, cyber risk and governance. Craig was an FBI Supervisory Special Agent prior to his private-sector roles, and helped establish the St. Louis FBI Cyber Task Force. Craig leads the St. Louis CISO board and is a founding member and adjunct professor for the Washington University in St. Louis Master of Cybersecurity Management program. He holds a doctorate, master's, and bachelor's degrees, along with Series 7 and 99 licenses.

name: Marc Child
bio: Marc Child is Director Information Security Assurance for Great River Energy where he applies extensive cyber, physical, personnel, and data security knowledge and three decades of leadership experience. At GRE, Marc is responsible for the holistic security program from design and implementation to compliance with North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Critical Infrastructure Protection regulations. Marc is a past Chair to the Critical Infrastructure Protection Committee at the NERC and is a current leader to the NERC Reliability and Security Technical Committee. Marc has earned both CISSP and GICSP certifications. Marc is an elected Executive Board member to the InfraGard Minnesota chapter and serves as Chair to the strategy committee and Vice Chair to the sector chief program. In 2021, Marc received the first Electricity Sector Security Service Award from the Electricity Information Sharing and Analysis Center (E-ISAC).

name: Sean Costigan
bio: Dr. Sean Costigan is an Operating Partner at Bluedge Ventures, focusing on investing in next-gen cybersecurity, AI, and emerging security solutions that strengthen resilience across public and private sectors. He drives strategic investments that help government and industry navigate evolving threats and build long-term security. As Senior Adviser for Emerging and Disruptive Technology at the NATO DEEP eAcademy, and as an author and board member, he contributes to guiding leaders, stewarding resources, and driving innovation at the intersection of security and technology. He leads NATO DEEP's curricular initiatives in cybersecurity, hybrid threats, and AI. In 2023, Dr. Costigan was honored with the Serge Lazareff Prize for his contributions to the Office of Legal Affairs of NATO SHAPE, reflecting his commitment to advancing security and resilience worldwide.

name: Tim Crothers
bio:
Tim is a cybersecurity executive with more than 40 years in technology and decades on the front lines of cyber defense.
Tim has led security at some of the world's most critical organizations, including serving as Chief Security Officer at Mandiant and leading global cyber defense at UnitedHealth Group. He's spent his career defending against nation-state and advanced threats—and building security programs that actually work in the real world.
Today, as CTO of CounterMeasure Security, he continues to challenge how we think about detection, response, and resilience.

name: Daniel Cunningham
bio: Dan Cunningham is Sr. Director and Deputy CISO at HealthPartners. Prior leadership roles include IT security management at Prime Therapeutics and cyber incident management for 3M. Dan was commissioned a Second Lieutenant in 2002 and Lieutenant Colonel Cunningham commanded at the company level, and was the first commander of the Minnesota Cyber Protection Team. He completed deployments to Bosnia in 2003-2004 and Iraq in 2006-2007 and 2009-2010. His most significant award includes the Bronze Star Medal with a bronze oak leaf cluster.

name: Kumar Dasani
bio: Kumar Dasani is the U.S. Region head of Info Sec responsible for cybersecurity strategy at B. Braun Medical, Inc. Known for collaborative leadership, he also advises security startups and is vCISO for Altheia. Kumar's broad experience includes cybersecurity strategy, preventive controls, privacy, and risk management across multiple critical infrastructure verticals. Kumar held executive financial services roles at Digital River and Deluxe, and led an enterprise security, business continuity and risk management program. He directed UnitedHealth Group policy and risk efforts, and at Medtronic he built a comprehensive cybersecurity program for a care management services division. Kumar earned a B.S. in computer science at St. Cloud State University and an M.S. in software systems at the University of St. Thomas in Minnesota and holds CIPP/US, CISA, CISM, CRISC, and CvCISO certifications. He received the Visionary Governance Risk and Compliance Leader and 2024 OnCon Top 100 Security Team Awards.

name: Loren Dealy Mahler
org: National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology
bio: Loren Dealy Mahler is Communications Director with the National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology. With over two decades of cybersecurity, defense, and emerging technology experience, Loren supports communications, government relations, and external engagement for public and private sector clients. Loren has advised established corporations and emerging startups, having split her career between greater New York and Washington, DC, where she worked at the White House, Department of Defense, and on Capitol Hill. Loren knows policy and politics, and her deep expertise enables her to navigate the complexities of business growth and security in today's dynamic landscape. Loren served as 2024 Co-Chair for the Cyber Security Summit (CSS) in Minneapolis.

name: Phil Englert
bio:
Phil Englert is the VP of Medical Device Security at Health-ISAC, where he works with medical device manufacturers to strengthen privacy and security while partnering with healthcare delivery organizations to ensure those solutions are practical, deployable, and clinically aligned. He also defines long-term vision, leads cross-sector initiatives, advances best practices, and delivers programs that improve sector resilience and serves as a subject-matter expert and contributor to Health-ISAC's Medical Device Security Council (MDSC). Phil leads Health-ISAC's strategy to strengthen cybersecurity and privacy across the global medical-technology ecosystem. This role directs the organization's medical device security program, partnering with manufacturers and healthcare delivery organizations to drive practical, secure implementations while shaping regulatory and standards. Phil oversees coordinated vulnerability disclosure efforts with researchers, regulators, and government agencies, and serves as a subject-matter expert to the 500-member Medical Device Security Council.
With more than 30 years of technical and operational leadership across healthcare and life sciences, Phil has led strategic direction-setting, operational improvement, and technology-enabled transformation initiatives. His previous roles include Chief Product Officer at MedSec, Global Leader for Medical Device Technology at Deloitte, Vice President of Operations at MDISS, and National Director of Technology Operations at Catholic Health Initiatives. He has also served as an executive leader for a $250M MedTech services organization supporting more than 130 acute-care facilities across 22 states, bringing deep knowledge of clinical environments, medical technologies, and maintenance operations.
Phil is widely recognized as a leading voice in MedTech cybersecurity and an active contributor to federal regulatory and standards efforts. His work spans MITA MDS2, NTIA SBOM, ISO 80001, MITRE's CVSS Medicalization group, ISA 99/IEC 62443, UL 2900, ISO TC215, AAMI TIR97, interoperability initiatives, HSCC Secure Supply Chain, and MDIC's 5G Healthcare working groups.

name: Chris Gabbard
bio: Christopher Gabbard is a Cybersecurity Advisor with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), assigned to Region V (IL, IN, MI, MN, OH & WI). Based in Minneapolis, Minnesota, he supports the mission of strengthening the security and resilience of the nation's critical infrastructure. Prior to joining CISA, Chris served as the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) for Ramsey County, Minnesota. Prior to being a CISO, Chris worked as an IT auditor and risk manager with PricewaterhouseCoopers, ING, and US Bank. Mr. Gabbard is a Certified Information Security Auditor (CISA), has Bachelor's Degrees in Accounting and Management Information System from the University of Northern Iowa.

name: Michelle Greeley
bio: Michelle Greeley is a Senior Director of Compliance at Solera Health and an accomplished professional with demonstrated proficiency in diverse management and leadership roles including experience in information security, security compliance, information technology, security incident response, data privacy, risk management, business continuity, disaster recovery, business technology planning, process engineering, project management, contract coordination, finance, and accounting. Michelle holds an MBA in Finance from the University of St. Thomas in Minnesota, and various industry certifications: CDPSE, CRISC, CGEIT, CISM, CISA, ITIL IT Service Management, Six Sigma Green Belt.

name: Tim Herman
bio:
Tim Herman is President of the InfraGard Minnesota Members Alliance, and an Enterprise Account Director at Online Business Systems where he helps organizations with digital transformation and cyber security services. Prior to OBS, Tim elevated preparedness for transportation, energy and other critical infrastructure clients through incident response planning and tabletop exercises.
Tim is a 2023 recipient of the Regional InfraGard Members Alliance Leadership Award, and an FBI Citizens Academy graduate. He has also served as a board member to the MN Information Systems Security Association.
Tim is passionate about industrial critical infrastructure security. At MBA Engineering, his work included specialized ICS/OT/IoT/IIoT/SCADA systems programming, integration, analytics, and cyber improvements. Tim has experience as a vCIO and Director of Client Strategy and Success for an IT managed services provider and spent more than ten years as President of SBC, a business strategy and consulting company.

name: Paul Hershberger
bio: Paul Hershberger is a cybersecurity executive with more than 25 years' experience currently responsible for Cybersecurity Threat management and Incident Response at nVent. Prior to nVent Paul provided leadership and direction to the enterprise team responsible for cyber threat identification and management at Cargill. Prior to Cargill, Paul led the development and implementation of a global security strategy as CISO for the Mosaic Company. Through the years Paul has held roles in technology risk consulting, infrastructure architecture, IT audit, and SOX compliance, and is a past chair to both the Food and Ag ISAC and Food and Ag Sector Coordinating Council. Prior to his cybersecurity career, Paul served in the US Army for 12 years.

name: John Israel
bio:
As the Chief Information Security Officer for the State of Minnesota, John Israel leads the executive branch cybersecurity teams within Minnesota IT Services (MNIT), the state information technology agency. The MNIT enterprise security office monitors, detects, and coordinates with key partners to prevent and respond to cyber threats that target state systems and services, and supports advanced cybersecurity defenses for local governments through state and local partnerships.
The office also supports cybersecurity planning and provides guidance to state executive branch agencies that connect Minnesotans to state services and programs every day. These teams have helped implement Governor Walz's Executive Order 22-20 on critical infrastructure cybersecurity, which calls on state agencies to prioritize resources to improve state network security and build strong collaboration, threat intelligence sharing, and cybersecurity awareness with critical infrastructure providers statewide.

name: Bill James
org: Navy League of the United States
bio: Bill James is the Midwest Region President of the Navy League of the United States. Bill has spent most of his career in high technology with F100 firms including Digital Equipment, HP, Sun Microsystems and AT&T Enterprise in strategic sales, marketing and senior management. His education tours include a BSMech Engr., from the University of Illinois and an MBA in Marketing and Finance from the Carlson Business School – U of MN.

name: Peter Kapelanski
bio: Peter Kapelanski is the Senior Manager for Vulnerability Vigilance in the Medtronic Product Security Office, leading a team that conducts penetration testing and cyber threat intelligence to protect Medtronic products. He previously worked as a principal security engineer. He is also a Lieutenant Colonel in the Minnesota Army National Guard, serving as the G-6 Communications Staff Officer for the 34th Infantry Division. His previous position was Commander of the 177th Cyber Protection Team. He has deployed twice, in support of Operations Enduring Freedom and Spartan Shield. He earned a B.S. in Industrial Engineering and Operations Research from the University of California, Berkeley. He also completed the MBA program at the University of Minnesota Carlson School of Management. His professional certifications include CISSP, CISM, OSCP, CEH, and PMP. He is the President of the Minnesota Chapter of the Military Cyber Professionals Association.

name: Lindsey Konerza
bio: Lindsey Konerza is a Security Governance and Awareness Analyst at the University of Minnesota, a top-tier Big Ten R1 research institution. She leads efforts to strengthen policies and procedures in line with compliance and regulatory frameworks, enhancing risk management practices and collaborating across teams on compliance initiatives. A passionate advocate for cybersecurity education, Lindsey develops and leads training sessions for the University community and drives awareness campaigns to foster a cybersecurity-conscious culture among faculty, staff, and students. Lindsey earned a Bachelor of Science in Biology from the University of Minnesota Duluth and a Master of Science in Security Technologies from the University of Minnesota Technological Leadership Institute.

name: Mamady Konneh
bio: Mamady Konneh is the Founder and Executive Director of WeNetworkNow, a non-profit that supports individuals from diverse backgrounds through mentorship and professional development programs. He currently leads a Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) program at Calabrio and previously led the Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) program at Okta. With over a decade of security industry experience across SaaS, healthcare, finance, and retail, Mamady shares his expertise as an adjunct faculty member at the University of Minnesota, where he teaches Cloud Security and Strategy. He authored a research paper on building a secure digital identification for Guinea Conakry, which he presented at an international conference in Marseille, France, in 2018. Mamady's commitment to fostering a community of changemakers earned him the 2021 Minnesota Outstanding Refugee Award. His work continues to bridge technology, education, and community to drive inclusive progress and innovation.

name: Patrick Kooiker
bio:
Patrick Kooiker, Chief Warrant Officer 2 (CW2), stands out as a distinguished cybersecurity professional whose journey seamlessly connects military cyber operations with leadership in the private sector. Currently, he serves as Director of Cybersecurity Governance and Risk at a Securian financial in the law and compliance department, where he leads three teams focused on legal compliance and fortifying cybersecurity programs. Patrick's expertise in risk management, governance, and cyber defense positions him as a critical protector of financial infrastructure.
Patrick's enthusiasm for engineering and technology is deeply ingrained, inspired by a family legacy. His father worked as a machinist and mechanic, while his mother, a doctorate-level IT engineer, modeled academic and professional excellence. Patrick's grandfather, an Army Air Corps aircraft mechanic and amphibious pilot, encouraged his early interest in aviation. By 17, Patrick had achieved his first solo flight, thanks to training with the Civil Air Patrol.
His teenage years saw him interning at Alliant Tech, working on shockwave analysis, and at Honeywell Avionics, where he contributed to the design of a laser gyroscope for the 737-400. These formative experiences laid the groundwork for his future in engineering and cybersecurity.
Patrick's military career began in 1995 in the U.S. Army Reserve as a Generator Mechanic. He later joined the Minnesota Air National Guard, earning two associate degrees and a bachelor's degree while traveling to more than forty countries and numerous U.S. states. His deployments included Iraq, the UAE, Korea, Germany, and more.
At Andrews Air Force Base, he worked on disaster relief after Hurricane Katrina. In 2009, as a federal contractor and lead engineer, he established secure communications in combat zones in Kyrgyzstan and Afghanistan. Patrick's unique military experiences include building a 200-foot communications tower and, on 9/11, assisting with the communications that scrambled F-16s for Air Force One, for which he was honored by President Bush and the Governor of Iowa.
Today, Patrick is integral to the Army National Guard's Defense Cyber Operations Element, leading a team at Joint Forces Headquarters. Notably, his team won first place at Cyber Shield 2023's SANS Netwar event. He also trains NATO nations in cybersecurity, with recent assignments in Croatia.
Patrick is dedicated to mentoring future Warrant Officers and serves as Director of Aerospace Education for the Minnesota Wing of the Civil Air Patrol, focusing on training cadets and advancing cybersecurity education. He also represents Minnesota Warrant Officers through the National Guard Association and is a Major in the Civil Air Patrol Auxiliary of the U.S. Air Force.
Outside his professional and military commitments, Patrick prioritizes family and personal well-being. His hobbies are diverse, including camping, fishing, backpacking, swimming, rucking, off-roading, coaching Special Olympics and adaptive baseball, and flying. He is deeply committed to his community and fostering the next generation of leaders.
Academic achievements: Associate degrees in Electronic Systems Technology and Information Systems Technology, Community College of the Air Force; Bachelor's in Applied Management (Information Systems Management), National American University.

name: David LaBelle
bio: David La Belle is a security analyst for the Federal Reserve. Prior to that, he worked as an analyst with Charter Solutions, after beginning his technology career with the United States Marine Corps. During his service he was tasked with various roles within the technology field for the U.S. Department of Defense, focusing on aviation and civilian systems. He was responsible for managing more than one million dollars in assets across several continents and served two tours in Iraq.

name: Phyllis Lee
bio: Phyllis Lee is the Vice President of Content Development at the Center for Internet Security (CIS). She has over 25 years of experience in information assurance and has performed vulnerability assessments, virtualization research and worked in security automation. Prior to joining CIS, Lee worked at the National Security Agency (NSA) focusing on the intersection between malware and virtualization, which included collaboration with MIT Lincoln Labs. Lee also participated in a variety of security automation standardization efforts and led the security automation strategy for the NSA Information Assurance Directorate (IAD). She graduated from Johns Hopkins University with a Master of Science in Computer Science.

name: Kristy Livingston
bio: Kristy Livingston is Senior Manager, Cybersecurity Operations at Sunrise Banks and an Adjunct Professor at Century College. She has 15 years of information security experience and has held leadership roles with oversight for data governance, vulnerability management, e-discovery and incident response teams. Kristy holds a Master of Science in Secure Technologies (MSST) from the University of Minnesota Technological Leadership Institute and maintains industry certifications including CISSP and EnCE.

name: Jennifer Lotze
bio: Jennifer Lotze is a principal consultant with IT Audit Labs and is the Northwest Region President for Women in Technology – Wisconsin and has held similar roles with the Wisconsin Educational Technology Leaders and the National Cyber Watch Center. Jennifer served as a Cyber Security Coordinator with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency where her mission-focused work strengthened critical infrastructure across Minnesota. Jennifer's passion for IT was developed during early days as a special education teacher, and she progressed to a senior technical leadership position in the Hudson, Wisconsin School District. To ensure equitable and accessible technology for all students, Jennifer led complex integration projects to give them a seamless experience across educational practices and platforms. Jennifer holds a Bachelor of Arts and a graduate degree from Carthage College in Wisconsin and is a Certified Educational Technology Leader and certified Google Education Trainer.

name: Eileen Manning
bio: Eileen Manning is a Founding Partner of the Cyber Security Summit and CEO of The Event Group Incorporated. With over 30 years as an entrepreneur, she specializes in strategic planning and marketing with a focus on technology events. In 2021, Eileen received the SANS Difference Maker Award in Security for her significant contributions to the field. Her career began at a leading advertising agency, followed by more than a decade at Prudential, where she produced hundreds of conferences for groups ranging from 100 to 5,000 attendees and managed regional corporate travel. Eileen's expertise spans production development, communications, public relations, video production, and graphic design. She has served on numerous boards and supports a broad range of professional associations and charitable organizations. Eileen is deeply committed to mentoring young professionals to shape the next generation of leaders, as her biggest strength is building community to protect our world's cyber space.

name: Tina Meeker
bio: Tina Meeker is Deputy CISO for Old Republic. Prior roles include Vice President of Information Security, Infrastructure and Enterprise Architecture at Sleep Number Corporation and leadership positions at Best Buy, Shutterfly, and Target. Tina is a highly credentialed executive with 20+ years of cybersecurity experience across financial, retail, manufacturing, technology, and medical device industries. She earned a BA in Organizational Behavior and Management from the College of St. Scholastica and an MBA from Augsburg University in Minnesota and holds a CISSP among other professional certifications. Ms. Meeker is a frequent guest lecturer and teacher for the next generation of cybersecurity professionals at various Minnesota universities and colleges and a featured speaker at industry conferences.

name: Jerrod Montoya
bio:
Jerrod is a trusted advisor to both C-suite executives and front-line teams, known for challenging the status quo while understanding when to operate within established rules. With more than a decade of experience at the intersection of law, security, and business, he helps organizations navigate complex cybersecurity and privacy challenges by aligning security controls with revenue strategies and positioning cybersecurity and privacy as enablers of business growth.
His strategies have helped professional sports teams transform their cyber programs, enabled a global health tech company to avoid millions in unnecessary compliance costs, and earned praise from a Silicon Valley retail executive who called his risk assessment "the best I've ever had."
Jerrod holds an M.S. in Security Technologies from the University of Minnesota's Technological Leadership Institute, a J.D. from Mitchell Hamline School of Law, and a B.A. in Political Science and Sociology from the University of Minnesota. He maintains an active Minnesota State Bar license and is a Certified Information Privacy Professional (CIPP) and Certified ISO 27001 Lead Implementer.

name: Brian Morgan
bio: Army Lieutenant Colonel Brian Morgan is the Director of the Cyber Coordination Cell (C3) for the Minnesota National Guard. He began his military career by enlisting in the Wisconsin Army National Guard before transferring to Minnesota, where he has held key roles in information security, networking, software, and cyber operations. LTC Morgan holds a bachelor's in applied mathematics and computer science from the University of Wisconsin-Stout and an MBA from the University of Saint Thomas in Minnesota. He is certified in CISSP, CISM, CEH, CCNA, CCSP, CNDA, PCEP, and AWS-CCP. Additionally, Morgan is the founder and past President of the Military Cyber Professionals Association (MCPA) Minnesota Chapter, a 501(c)(3) organization focused on developing cyber talent and advancing STEM education.

name: Michael Nghiem
bio: Michael Nghiem is a Product Manager of Identity and Access Management at Edward Jones, supporting a multi-year security modernization journey to protect the firm's clients, branches, and home offices. Previously, he advised Fortune 500 clients in PwC's Cybersecurity and Privacy practice across industries such as financial services, telecommunications, healthcare, and retail. Passionate about the intersection of business and national security policy, Michael was the Summit's first intern 16 years ago, an experience he credits with shaping his career, and returns to advance cross-sector cybersecurity collaboration through the Think Tank.

name: David Notch
bio: David Notch is Chief Information Security Officer for Castlelake, L.P., an investment firm that specializes in complex, asset-rich and cash-flowing opportunities in undercapitalized or inefficient private markets using investment strategies in real assets, specialty finance and aviation. David uses his 30 years of technology and security experience to lead the cybersecurity, technology infrastructure, facilities and technology vendor management programs for Castlelake.

name: Eric Ong
bio: Eric Ong is Senior Director, Global Information Security at Donaldson. With more than 25 years of experience in IT, Eric is a passionate, tech-savvy, and business-minded security leader who drives enterprise-wide cyber defense initiatives while fostering a culture of collaboration. He builds and empowers global teams to deliver innovative and compliant solutions.

name: Nicole Pruden
bio: Nicole Pruden is Network and Security Administrator at ECMECC.

name: Dan Rieken
bio: Dan Rieken is a Principal Cybersecurity Engineer at EMCUBE, Inc. Once a Naval reservist, Dan graduated from the University of Minnesota with a degree in Aerospace Engineering & Mechanics and retired from the Navy as an Information Professional officer and member of the Space Cadre. Dan was an Associate Fellow on the CNO Strategic Studies Group and earned a Master's degree from the Naval Postgraduate School and a National Security Studies Certificate from the Naval War College. Dan's engineering and leadership positions with the Navy and Department of Defense include Secretary of the Navy staff and White House Communication Agency Presidential Communication Officer. Dan develops cyber test and evaluation policy and guidance, assessing cyber engineering, planning and execution efforts for acquisition programs.

name: Shawn Riley
bio: Shawn Riley is co-founder and CEO of BISBLOX, a venture studio that helps companies around the world to be bold, disrupt boring and strengthen growth. A lifelong technologist and entrepreneur, Shawn started his first company at the age of 16, and over time became a thought leader for big-brand companies including IBM and Mayo Clinic. His career story is a string of transformational change chapters that span multi-billion-dollar organizations, through a variety of C-level roles, including Chief Executive Officer, Chief Information Officer, Chief Technology Officer, and Information Management Officer. In 2017 Shawn was appointed by North Dakota Governor Doug Burgum to serve the state as Chief Information Officer and cabinet member. Today, known for his energy and a focus on the future, Shawn travels the globe with the Bisblox mission at the fore, asking "How might we help others succeed?"

name: Mark Ritchie
bio: Former Minnesota Secretary of State Mark Ritchie now serves as a Civilian Aide to the Secretary of the Army for Minnesota and as a senior advisor to Anubis Consulting. Mark previously served as President of Global Minnesota, one of the nation's oldest and largest global-minded civic organizations working to advance international understanding and engagement. Mark has a long history of dedicated public service roles as Board Chair of World's Fair Fund, National Secretary of the U.S. Election Assistance Commission Advisory Board, and as a member of Minnesota's Board of Investment and Executive Council.

name: Eric Roeske
bio: Captain Eric Roeske is the Director of Capitol Security and Executive Protection division of the Minnesota State Patrol, with more than 25 years of law enforcement experience at the municipal, county and state level. During his time with the Minnesota State Patrol, he has been a patrol trooper, SWAT team member, firearms and crowd management instructor and public information officer. Captain Roeske holds a bachelor's degree in sociology from the University of Wisconsin-River Falls and a Master's of Science in Security Technologies from the University of Minnesota Technological Leadership Institute.

name: Michael Rogers
bio: Michael Rogers is CISO and Director of Security and Compliance at Hormel Foods, where he applies more than 25 years of technology experience and information security leadership. Mike has held a variety of roles in infrastructure engineering/architecture, secure development, compliance, access management, and cyber defense. Mike earned his MBA from the University of Minnesota Carlson School of Management and is passionate about business and IT risk, studying incentives, and helping others reach their potential. He lives in St. Paul with his wife and two spoiled dogs.

name: Scott Singer
bio: Scott Singer is President of ControlCase. He retired from the U.S. Navy as a Captain after serving 30+ years in active duty and reserve roles. Earlier in his career, Scott was CIO at PaR Systems, and worked at Medtronic as European Infrastructure Manager, Vascular division CIO, and head of global security. Scott has experience with regulatory frameworks, government contracts, Federal Acquisition Regulations, HIPAA, med device, cybersecurity, aerospace and nuclear matters. His board work includes the Minnesota Technology Association, UW-Madison NROTC Alumni Association, and Minnesota InfraGard. Scott has an MBA in Information Systems from the University of Minnesota, Carlson School of Management, and a BS in Meteorology from the University of Wisconsin – Madison. He holds a certification in Joint Professional Military Education from The Naval War College, and holds CMMC Assessor, Professional and Provisional Instructor Certifications.

name: Justin Smith
bio:
Justin Smith is a Principal Security Architect at Ecolab with more than twenty years of experience leading security strategy. He drives security reviews of Ecolab's integration of agentic solutions in our various platforms and has built out a comprehensive threat and vulnerability management program. Throughout his career, he has consistently aligned cybersecurity capabilities with business objectives and operational resilience.
In addition to his corporate leadership, Justin serves in the Minnesota Army National Guard as a Cyber Warfare Warrant Officer, supporting Army cyber operations and advising senior leaders on defensive cyber strategy. He was the first approved Cyber Warrant Officer packet in the State of Minnesota and is also a member of the Military Cyber Professionals Association (MCPA) Minnesota Chapter, a 501(c)(3) organization focused on developing cyber talent and advancing STEM education.
Justin holds a Master of Security Technologies from the University of Minnesota and maintains numerous industry certifications, including the CISSP and CISM.

name: Rachel Soanes
bio: Rachel Soanes is Vice President of Operations and a member of the executive leadership team at BL King Consulting, where she leads operational strategy, business transformation, and technology enablement initiatives. She also serves on the Board of Directors for the InfraGard Minnesota Chapter, supporting collaboration focused on cybersecurity awareness and critical infrastructure resilience.

name: Tony Taylor
bio: Tony Taylor has held multiple infrastructure and security related roles throughout his career and is currently the CISO for Land O'Lakes, Inc. Under Taylor's direction, the IT infrastructure and security functions have transformed from a business unit environment to an enterprise shared service, serving all divisions of Land O'Lakes.

name: Stacy Tietjen
bio: Stacy Tietjen is an adjunct professor at the St. Thomas School of Law in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Recent past work includes Senior Director of Compliance and Integrity for CHS Inc., a leading global agribusiness owned by farmers, ranchers and cooperatives across the United States, where she led compliance programs across the company, with responsibilities that include the Code of Conduct, policies, training, investigations, compliance and integrity initiatives, and the enterprise record and information management program. Stacy has served on numerous boards including Secure360 | Upper Midwest Security Alliance (UMSA), Minnesota Agricultural and Rural Leadership (MARL), Business Continuity Planners Association (BCPA), and the FBI Minneapolis Citizens Academy Alumni Association (FBIMCAAA). She earned a Bachelor of Arts in Information Technology and a Master of Arts in Leadership and Management from Concordia University in St. Paul, Minnesota.

name: Shayla Treadwell
bio: Dr. Shayla Treadwell is Deputy Chief Security Officer at Lumen Technologies. In this role, Dr. Treadwell oversees the company's information security programs and helps drive stakeholder collaboration on issues related to information technology governance, risk, compliance, and assurance. Previously, Dr. Treadwell was Vice President of Governance, Risk, and Compliance at ECS and led the cybersecurity risk management program to ensure alignment to security regulations, frameworks, and certifications.

name: Anaya Twum
bio: Anaya Twum, MBA, is an IT Project Manager at 3M focused on cybersecurity, data privacy, and technology governance. She leads enterprise initiatives aligning secure software development with compliance frameworks. Anaya serves as a board member of TeamWomen, a professional development network committed to empowering girls and women from the classroom to the C-suite. She also leads professional development programming for PMI-MN and is passionate about the intersection of cybersecurity, enterprise transformation, and expanding access to technology education.

name: Paul Veeneman
bio: Paul Veeneman is President of the Information Systems Security Association Minnesota chapter. With over 27 years of experience across various industries including finance, oil and gas, healthcare and manufacturing, Paul has been actively working within the Nation's critical infrastructure, addressing challenges, providing guidance, insight and innovation in Operations Technology, Industrial Controls, IoT, IIoT, SCADA cyber security knowledge, expertise, and education. Paul holds CISSP, CISM, and CRISC certifications, and his board work extends beyond the ISSA chapter to include the InfraGard Minnesota Members Alliance and the International Society of Automation (ISA) local chapter.

name: Nikki Weis
bio: Nicolette Weis is a Cyber Officer in the Minnesota Air National Guard and a Planner for the Minnesota National Guard's Cyber Coordination Cell (C3), where she supports cyber preparedness and incident response partnerships across Minnesota. With prior enlisted experience and over a decade of military service, her work focuses on cybersecurity readiness, training, and collaboration across state and federal partners. Nicolette also serves on the board of the Minnesota chapter of the Military Cyber Professionals Association (MCPA).

name: Bob Weiss
bio: Bob Weiss is the secretary of the ISC2 Twin Cities chapter and an experienced cybersecurity professional. He is founder and principal of WyzCo Group Inc., where he provides consulting on security products and services, and performs security audits, compliance audits, vulnerability assessments, and penetration tests. Bob also teaches Cybersecurity Awareness Training and works as an IT and cybersecurity instructor for various training and certification organizations. His diverse experience spans corporate, military, government, and workforce development environments. As a seasoned speaker, Bob has presented at several Secure360 conferences, the 2016 ISC2 World Congress, and the 2017 ISSA International Conference. Find his blogs back to 2006 at WyzGuysCyberSecurity.com.

name: Troy Wilkinson
bio:
Troy Wilkinson is CEO of CYPRO and is a cybersecurity executive, former Fortune 500 Chief Information Security Officer, and recognized thought leader in cyber defense and digital trust. Over the course of his career, he has built and led global cybersecurity programs that protect critical infrastructure, intellectual property, and enterprise systems in an increasingly complex threat landscape.
Earlier in his career, Troy served as an international cybercrime investigator, working on cross-border digital crime cases that shaped his perspective on the global nature of cyber threats and the importance of collaboration between governments and industry.
Today, he advises cybersecurity startups and works closely with security leaders and venture investors to connect real-world challenges with emerging innovation. A frequent speaker at global conferences, Troy focuses on the intersection of cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and leadership, helping organizations navigate the rapidly evolving risks and opportunities of the digital era.

name: Dr. Massoud Amin
bio: Dr. Massoud Amin, IEEE and ASME Fellow, is president of Energy Policy and Security Associates, an emeritus Professor, Director, and Honeywell H.W. Sweatt Chair in Technological Leadership, and a University Distinguished Teaching Professor Award Recipient, at the University of Minnesota. He is widely credited as being the "father of the smart grid", and a cyber-physical security leader, who led the development of 24 technologies transferred to industry and directed all security-related R&D for all North American utilities after the 9/11 tragedies. In fact, he was at a meeting less than a mile from the Pentagon, discussing disaster risk management with White House OSTP, U.S. DoD officials, and representative of other agencies when the terrorist attacks took place on September 11, 2001.

name: Anne Bader
bio:
Anne C. Bader is Principal, Bader Resources, LLC, Founder of The International Cybersecurity Dialogue, a Senior Associate Fellow of the Institute of Statecraft, London and an Associate Expert, Defense Security Emergence Team (EESD) Cnam, Paris.
Previously, Mrs. Bader served as a Senior Research Fellow and Director, Advanced Research Assessment Group, The Defence Academy of The United Kingdom, UK; Visiting Programme Director, Wilton Park; Executive Vice President, The Fund for Peace; Vice President of the Atlantic Council of the United States; Trinity College and Business Executives for National Security, US.
A citizen of Canada and the United States, she received a NATO award and is an Honorary Citizen of Hungary.

name: Andrew Borene
bio: Andrew Borene is President and CEO of a new combat robotics company and maker of more than 7,000 fielded "Throwbot" systems used by military, law enforcement and public safety agencies worldwide. Prior executive roles include global security director at Flashpoint, a threat intelligence firm and leadership positions at Fortune 500 firms that include IBM, Symantec, Booz Allen Hamilton, LexisNexis, and Wells Fargo. In government, Andrew was a senior staff officer at the National Counterterrorism Center (NCTC) and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), an associate deputy general counsel at the Pentagon, an advisor at CIA, and he is a Marine Corps combat veteran. Andrew is a nonprofit board member with Special Operations Association of America and the European Marshall Center Partnership for Peace Consortium. He has a JD from the University of Minnesota Law School and a BA in Economics from Macalester College in St. Paul, Minnesota. He is a past recipient of the FBI Director's Award and the ODNI Exceptional Achievement Award.

name: Steen Fjalstad
bio: Steen Fjalstad works for the Midwest Reliability Organization (MRO) as part of the Critical Infrastructure Protection team helping to secure the North American Electric Grid. Working for MRO Steen has managed, led, and supported security work with numerous North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) registered entities on critical infrastructure protection. Steen coordinates with industry, local, state, and federal agencies to manage outreach efforts on threats & vulnerabilities to the Grid. Prior to joining MRO, Steen obtained significant experience as a security, audit, risk, and project manager with a focus on securing, designing, implementing, and auditing technology systems. Steen has served over two hundred different organizations spanning three continents. Steen holds a Master's of Science in Security Technologies from the University of Minnesota, and a Bachelor's degree in Computer Management Systems from the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater.

name: Stefanie Horvath
bio: Stefanie Horvath, CISSP, is the Chief Information Security Officer at the City of Saint Paul where she is responsible for securing the City's data, applications and networks. She also serves in the Army National Guard and currently serves as the Deputy Commanding General for the Army's Cyber Center of Excellence. Her most significant awards include the Defense Service Medal, the Bronze Star Medal and the Meritorious Service Medal. Major General Horvath holds a Master's Degree in Strategic Studies from the United States Army War College and Master's Degree in Cybersecurity from the EC-Council. Horvath received the Cyber Security Summit Visionary Governance Champion award in 2018 and served for many years on the CSS Think Tank/Advisory Board.

name: Brian Isle
bio:
Brian Isle, P.E., is the co-founder and former CEO of Adventium Labs, and a Senior Fellow at Technological Leadership Institute teaching courses in information assurance and risk assessment. Brian continues his research on critical infrastructure safety and security, building on two decades of security-related experience. Brian was a key team member for the Food Protection and Defense Institute on a DHS-funded program to improve cyber security in food manufacturing. Brian supported the DOE-funded NESCOR program to improve the cyber security readiness of the next generation power grid. Brian held key roles on a DoD program focused on vulnerability assessment for force protection and a DHS program to apply advanced cyber protection technology to control systems for critical infrastructure.
Brian was honored with the 2016 Visionary Leader Award by the Cyber Security Summit. Brian is on the Board of Advisers for the Cyber Security Summit. Brian is a professional engineer registered in Minnesota. Brian is a member of the Minnesota chapter of the FBI sponsored InfraGard, ASIS International, ISA, and IEEE.

name: Mike Johnson
bio: Mike Johnson is past Honeywell James J. Renier chair in security technologies and former senior fellow at the Technological Leadership Institute at the University of Minnesota where he was responsible for developing security curriculum for the security technologies master's degree program, driving critical infrastructure protection and security industry issues discussions and training future security leaders. Mike has also spent more than 25 years as a security and risk management leader in the corporate environment.

name: Mike Kearn
bio: Mike Kearn is a Business Information Security Officer (BISO) within U.S. Bank Information Security Services. Within his role, he regularly consults with senior technology and operational risk management executives as an information security subject matter expert. Through this collaborative partnership, he drives the integration of sound security practices into the strategic roadmaps for his clients. Mr. Kearn brings more than 23 years of varied experience in information technology and security to his current role.

name: Gregory Ogdahl
bio: Lieutenant Colonel Greg Ogdahl is the Total Forces Integration Officer for the U.S. Cyber Command Cyber National Mission Force (CNMF) and aligns Reserve Component capabilities with CNMF mission requirements, develops readiness training programs, and advises senior leaders on the Department of Defense Total Force Policy. LTC Ogdahl fosters collaboration between Active and Reserve Components to strengthen national cybersecurity operations. He holds a B.S. in Business Computer Information Systems from St. Cloud State University and an M.S. in Management of Technology from the University of Minnesota and a graduate of the Joint and Combined Warfighting School at the Joint Forces Staff College. A seasoned leader, LTC Ogdahl applies cyber operations, information security and strategic skills and maintains Boardroom Certified Qualified Technology Expert (QTE), Certified Information Security Manager (CISM), and Certified Ethical Hacker (C|EH) credentials.

name: Tony Sager
bio: Tony Sager is a Senior VP and Chief Evangelist for the Center for Internet Security. He leads the development of the CIS Critical Security Controls, a worldwide consensus project to find and support technical best practices in cybersecurity. Tony also serves as the Director of the SANS Innovation Center, a subsidiary of The SANS Institute.

name: Catharine Trebnick
bio: Catharine Trebnick is Managing Director at Rosenblatt Securities and a leading expert on cloud and infrastructure security, and unified communications. Prior to working as a sell side equity analyst Ms. Trebnick held multiple senior leadership roles at Roth Capital Partners, Colliers International, Time Warner Telecom, Level 3 Communications, and AT&T. Ms. Trebnick earned a Bachelor of Science in chemistry with a minor in chemical engineering from University of Maryland. She also earned a Master of Business degree from the University of Chicago in Illinois. Ms. Trebnick is a frequent guest on CNBC and has received acclaim for her research in Barron's, Wall Street Journal, Reuters, Bloomberg, TheStreet.com, Forbes, Investor's Business Daily and CNNMoney.

name: John Valente
bio: John Valente serves as a CXO Executive Advisor for Zscaler and is a member to the board of advisors for Pacer Center. John has a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Fairfield University in Fairfield, Connecticut. His professional IT career included work for Citibank, Pepsi, Dell, Best Buy, and 3M, before his retirement in late 2019. John's career was focused mainly on information technology infrastructure, architecture and management.

name: Chris Veltsos
bio: Chris, aka Dr.InfoSec, is passionate about helping organizations take stock of their cyber risks and manage those risks across the intricate landscape of technology, business, and people.
